Hi Ana / Medicus legal team,

Thanks again for the detailed questions on the Private deployment (VPC) BYOK model. We reviewed the request from your procurement and legal teams and put together a proposed set of escrow release conditions and a scoped approach for subprocessor notification that we think balances legal defensibility with operational safety.

High level proposal (attached: redwood_escrow_procedure_draft.pdf, proposed_subprocessor_matrix.csv):
- Escrow release triggers: (1) court order or binding legal process; (2) joint written agreement signed by Medicus and Redwood (timeout window 30 days to resolve); (3) insolvency/liquidation event with independent trustee review. No unilateral remote-release mechanism.
- Evidence package required prior to any release: notarized request from customer legal, proof of identity for the custodian, signed attestation from Redwood verifying no remaining contractual cures, and a forensics snapshot (audit log excerpt) showing keystore state.
- Operator access (breakglass): operator sessions can be enabled only after both (a) dual authorization from Redwood security and Medicus designated approver and (b) real-time recorded session with immutable audit trail. Access windows should be time-limited and require signed post-access attestation.
- Subprocessor scoping & notification: we will publish a minimal list of subprocessors that may have visibility into infra telemetry (not customer plaintext data). Any addition to that list outside the announced set requires 30-day notice and an opportunity for Medicus to object/require mitigations.
- Data transfer safe harbor: for cross-border support we propose SRR-style contractual safeguards + SCCs as needed; no key material leaves customer-controlled HSMs except under the escrow conditions above.

Open items we want your input on: acceptable escrow evidence items, acceptable timing for operator sessions, and whether Medicus requires a notarized third-party trustee as part of the release workflow.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call Friday (11/17) to walk through the procedure and the attachment line items?

Cheers,

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Counsel, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_escrow_procedure_draft.pdf (15 pages, draft), proposed_subprocessor_matrix.csv (preview 3 rows)

Hannah,

Helpful summary — thanks. A couple quick clarifying asks from our side before the call:

1) When you say "forensics snapshot (audit log excerpt)", can you outline the exact minimum fields Redwood will provide? We need chain-of-custody for the request.
2) The dual authorization model: would Medicus be able to designate more than one approver (we often rotate approvers for coverage)?
3) Trustee: Medicus legal prefers an independent trustee for escrow releases in insolvency scenarios. Can Redwood provide a list of trustees you have used before or confirm you have a trustee partner?

Also copying our procurement lead Ana for confirmation on the 30-day subprocessor notice.

Quick follow-up from an ops/controls perspective — adding a few concrete answers to Carlos's questions so the call can focus on policy tradeoffs: 

- Audit snapshot minimum fields: timestamp (UTC), request_id, operator_identity (Redwood session id), keystore_id, action_type (export/import/rotate), hash of key material (SHA256) to verify state without revealing key, signed Redwood service attestation (PKCS7). These are produced automatically by the runtime when a km operation is initiated and are retained for 365 days by default; retention can be adjusted by contract.
- Approver rotation: yes, Medicus can maintain a set of designated approvers (up to 5) and designate one or more delegates; each approver's identity must be a verifiable corporate email and we require a primary and secondary approver for redundancy. Authorization logic requires two distinct approvers for operator breakglass.
- Trustee: Redwood currently partners with two third-party trustees for custody and escrow (we can share redacted references). Trustee involvement only occurs under insolvency/forced-release paths; for court order paths the trustee acts as verifier of request authenticity.
- Operator sessions: sessions are recorded, end-to-end integrity protected and shipped to customer S3 (or shared secure bucket) immediately after the session. We propose a default 7-day retention for session video/logs unless Medicus requires longer.

I added primitives in the attached CSV for the proposed subprocessor classification: telemetry-only, metadata-moderate, and config-admin (customer-controlled keys excluded).

Happy to talk through the file during the call.

- Priyom
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Ana / Carlos —

Thanks for the quick read and the thoughtful questions. Confirming next steps and proposed playbook items before our call Monday: 

1) Redwood will produce a redlined escrow procedure that: enumerates the exact audit fields (per Priyom's note), names the two trustee partners (redacted references) and shows the dual-approver flow diagram.
2) Medicus to confirm approver roster and whether trustee involvement is required for non-insolvency paths (if yes, we will include trustee onboarding checklist).
3) Procurement: Medicus to confirm whether 30-day notice for new subprocessors is acceptable, and if you want any subprocessors subject to pre-approval (we can convert the "config-admin" class to "pre-approval required" for sensitive partners).
4) Operational defaults: session recordings retained 7 days by default; audit logs retained 365 days (contract-adjustable).
